details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorms developing along the Front Range will evolve eastward through this evening, bringing a risk for isolated severe wind gusts and large hail

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest surface analysis depicts a cold front approaching the Front Range across portions of the central High Plains. Easterly, upslope flow within the post-frontal air mass is aiding in the westerly advection of richer low-level moisture (low-to-mid 60s F surface dewpoints). As thunderstorms developing along the Front Range evolve eastward and encounter this greater moisture and buoyancy, at least some increase in the severe risk is expected. Modest effective shear of 20-30 kts (indicated by recent mesoanalysis) and cold pool consolidation should primarily favor a multicellular/cluster storm mode, with damaging/severe wind gusts the primary hazard owing to steep low-level lapse rates. Isolated large hail may also accompany any more robust updrafts given the presence of steeper mid-level lapse rates. Watch issuance appears unlikely at this time owing to the expectation for the severe risk to remain generally limited in coverage and magnitude

details.label: Summary
details.text: A threat of severe wind gusts and marginal hail will persist into central to southern Indiana

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cluster of storms on the southern periphery of the dying MCS has remained relatively strong/persistent today across central IL, and is now moving into IN. These storms continue to track along the instability gradient, with access to a very moist air mass (PWAT > 2.20") and around 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Recent radar trends show other storms developing ahead/southeast of the main storm cluster, indicative of the uncapped air mass. Low-level wind fields are weak, but at least some rightward propagation is possible into the peak heating hours. Localized severe wind gusts will remain the main threat, though marginal hail may occur from time to time

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: High-based thunderstorms will develop across portions of the central High/Great Plains this afternoon and bring a risk for isolated severe wind gusts

details.label: Summary
details.text: High-based thunderstorms will develop across portions of the central High/Great Plains this afternoon and bring a risk for isolated severe wind gusts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest visible satellite imagery depicts a deepening cumulus field within a plume of very steep low-level lapse rates of 10+ C/km (per latest objective analysis) across portions of the TX/OK Panhandles to the south of a frontal system analyzed across CO/KS. Recent observations indicate this air mass has warmed into the low 100s F with dewpoints ranging from the mid-50s (Panhandles) to mid-60s F (Kansas). Regional 18z observed soundings from AMA/DDC sampled this environment and depicted deep, increasingly well-mixed boundary layer profiles with weak deep-layer flow/shear (less than 10-15 kts). While this will generally limit the organization developing, high-based convection, efficient evaporative cooling and cold pool formation will foster a risk for at least isolated severe wind gusts to 65-70 mph given inverted-V thermodynamic profiles. This threat may locally increase with northward extent where storms will encounter greater low-level moisture and buoyancy to the north of a surface cold front. Trends will continue to be monitored, but generally limited potential for storm organization and the isolated nature of the severe risk are likely to preclude watch issuance

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms will bring a risk for isolated damaging/severe wind gusts and perhaps an instance or two of marginally severe hail to portions of the Great Basin through this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Aided by ascent ahead of an upper-level trough centered over California, thunderstorm development is ongoing across portions of central and southern Nevada and along the Sierra Nevada Mountains in eastern California. Strong diurnal heating, modestly cool temperatures aloft, and surface dewpoints around 50 F are supporting weak buoyancy, with 500-1000 J/kg MLCAPE depicted by latest objective analysis and the 18 UTC VEF observed sounding. As thunderstorms evolve northeastward through this evening, steepening low-level lapse rates and increasingly well-mixed boundary layer profiles will promote evaporatively cooled downdrafts and cold pool formation. In conjunction with modest effective shear of 20-25 kts, this is expected to result in loosely organized convective clusters and an isolated risk for damaging/severe wind gusts. An instance or two of marginally severe hail also cannot be ruled out with the most robust updrafts. Given the expectation for the severe risk to remain limited in magnitude, watch issuance appears unlikely at this time
